q1_who.name: q1_who
q1_who.value: OVS S.p.A. is Italy's leading value/mass apparel retailer (menswear, womenswear, kidswear, plus underwear, beauty and home decor), running a vertically integrated model across the full value chain with a platform of proprietary brands. Tier: MASS / value (price points e.g. dresses €15–35 for the OVS core line, with premium sub-brands like GAP/PIOMBO reaching €80–100). Channel mix: DTC-led via 2,600+ stores (mostly OVS, Upim, Goldenpoint banners) plus e-commerce and franchise/wholesale. Markets: Italy core, with international franchise expansion (Japan, Mexico, India, Dubai). Listed on Euronext Milan since 2015; standalone group (no parent), >9,000 employees. Own-brand portfolio includes PIOMBO, OVS Kids, Blukids, Stefanel, Les Copains, Shaka and CROFF.

q2_direction.name: q2_direction
q2_direction.value: Direction: INNOVATING / INVESTING — copy-what-works, then propose scale. Live PDP imagery (Jan 2026 sample) is a clean, structured, on-model-led shot set: ~3 on-model views per SKU (L/F/R) on consistent studio-grey/white backgrounds, plus 1–2 still-life packshots and occasional short-form video (_V1). This is markedly more on-model and more consistent than the largely packshot/category-tile presentation visible in the ~2023 Wayback snapshot. OVS is clearly putting money into imagery and digital, not lagging — reinforced by a €33m Puglia technology/innovation hub explicitly targeting digital transformation, AI and cybersecurity. Triggers: ongoing digital-innovation capex, Goldenpoint integration, new sub-brand launches (B.Angel, Utopja, Altavia) and international franchise expansion (India, Dubai). Recommendation: do NOT pitch a visual overhaul; lead with scale/throughput on an already-good visual system.

q3_momentum.name: q3_momentum
q3_momentum.value: GROWING (brand and group aligned — OVS is standalone, so no brand-vs-parent split). FY2025 (year to Jan 2026): net sales €1,746M, up ~7% YoY (≈3% organic + Goldenpoint acquisition), adjusted EBITDA €218M, up ~20%. Growth is broad-based: Q3 2025 net sales +9% YoY, 9M 2025 +5.8%; womenswear (Les Copains, PIOMBO) and beauty (doubled since 2021, now ~8% of OVS sales) outperforming; international franchise (India, Dubai) delivering strong density. Cash generation guided up ~20% to €80–85M. One watch-item: the Kasanova acquisition was allowed to lapse (conditions unmet), and management flags a still-uncertain market. Net financial position adjusted ~€(146)M — manageable at ~0.8x EBITDA leverage.

gap.name: gap
gap.value: THROUGHPUT, not quality — and that's the whole point with OVS. They already shoot a clean, on-model-led studio set (~5 AI-amenable shots/SKU, ~67% on-model, consistent grey/white backgrounds) in-house, so 'cut your photo budget' is the wrong wedge: per-image cost is already low. The real constraint is volume velocity — ~3,563 live women's-apparel SKUs and an estimated ~40k new SKUs/yr feeding an in-house, vertically integrated studio that is structurally at capacity, while three banners (OVS/Upim/Goldenpoint) plus franchise markets (Japan, Mexico, India, Dubai) each need their own variants. Sartiq's single wedge: elastic AI on-model + still-life capacity that absorbs new-arrival surges and produces marketplace/banner/localized variants at near-zero marginal cost, freeing the studio to lead on craft instead of grinding on volume.

strategy.name: strategy
strategy.value: Scale-the-studio play (mass/value retailer, brand and group aligned, both GROWING — OVS is standalone, no parent split). Do NOT pitch a visual overhaul or cost displacement: their imagery is already good and their studio is in-house, so the modeled €8.0–47.2M is an agency-rate upper bound that overstates pure savings. Sell speed and localization, not savings. Position Sartiq as overflow capacity on top of an already-good visual system. Anchor credibility to OVS's own €33m Puglia digital/AI hub — they're already buying into AI-enabled operations, so this is an extension of stated strategy, not a leap. Open the relationship on new-arrival surge velocity and zero-marginal-cost localization across banners and franchise markets as the concrete, sizable levers.

We add elastic on-model and still-life capacity that absorbs new-arrival surges and spins up marketplace and localized variants for OVS/Upim/Goldenpoint and your franchise markets at near-zero marginal cost, so the studio leads on craft instead of grinding on volume. input.name: q1_who
input.value: OVS S.p.A. is Italy's leading value/mass apparel retailer (menswear, womenswear, kidswear, plus underwear, beauty and home decor), running a vertically integrated model across the full value chain with a platform of proprietary brands. Tier: MASS / value (price points e.g. dresses €15–35 for the OVS core line, with premium sub-brands like GAP/PIOMBO reaching €80–100). Channel mix: DTC-led via 2,600+ stores (mostly OVS, Upim, Goldenpoint banners) plus e-commerce and franchise/wholesale. Markets: Italy core, with international franchise expansion (Japan, Mexico, India, Dubai). Listed on Euronext Milan since 2015; standalone group (no parent), >9,000 employees. Own-brand portfolio includes PIOMBO, OVS Kids, Blukids, Stefanel, Les Copains, Shaka and CROFF.

input.name: q2_direction
input.value: Direction: INNOVATING / INVESTING — copy-what-works, then propose scale. Live PDP imagery (Jan 2026 sample) is a clean, structured, on-model-led shot set: ~3 on-model views per SKU (L/F/R) on consistent studio-grey/white backgrounds, plus 1–2 still-life packshots and occasional short-form video (_V1). This is markedly more on-model and more consistent than the largely packshot/category-tile presentation visible in the ~2023 Wayback snapshot. OVS is clearly putting money into imagery and digital, not lagging — reinforced by a €33m Puglia technology/innovation hub explicitly targeting digital transformation, AI and cybersecurity. Triggers: ongoing digital-innovation capex, Goldenpoint integration, new sub-brand launches (B.Angel, Utopja, Altavia) and international franchise expansion (India, Dubai). Recommendation: do NOT pitch a visual overhaul; lead with scale/throughput on an already-good visual system.

input.name: q3_momentum
input.value: GROWING (brand and group aligned — OVS is standalone, so no brand-vs-parent split). FY2025 (year to Jan 2026): net sales €1,746M, up ~7% YoY (≈3% organic + Goldenpoint acquisition), adjusted EBITDA €218M, up ~20%. Growth is broad-based: Q3 2025 net sales +9% YoY, 9M 2025 +5.8%; womenswear (Les Copains, PIOMBO) and beauty (doubled since 2021, now ~8% of OVS sales) outperforming; international franchise (India, Dubai) delivering strong density. Cash generation guided up ~20% to €80–85M. One watch-item: the Kasanova acquisition was allowed to lapse (conditions unmet), and management flags a still-uncertain market. Net financial position adjusted ~€(146)M — manageable at ~0.8x EBITDA leverage.

input.name: q5_pdp
input.value: Current PDP imagery is a structured, on-model-led studio system on a Salesforce Commerce Cloud (Demandware) platform. Per-SKU shot set (from JSON-LD + live classification of a 21-image women's-dress sample): ~3 on-model views (L/F/R) + 1–2 still-life packshots (FSTILL/D1STILL) + 1–3 detail shots (D1/D2/D3), with occasional short-form video (_V1) — roughly 6–7 raw images, of which ~5 are AI-amenable on-model/still-life. Mix among classified shots: ~67% on-model, ~33% still-life, video present but rare. Backgrounds are consistent studio-grey / plain-white; consistency rated medium (some variance grey vs white across SKUs). Cross-channel note: same DC-hosted images are reused on marketplaces/banners, with occasional quality downgrade vs own site. Net: quality is already good and on-model-heavy — the constraint is throughput/volume and localization, not visual quality.

Sartiq's wedge = elastic AI on-model + still-life capacity for surge throughput and near-zero-marginal-cost localization, so the studio leads on craft instead of grinding on volume.
